1 of 5. Priya uploads a batch of orders for the Pune branch. Some orders name a customer, 'Sharma Traders', who is on Pune's customer list but not on head office's list. What should happen?
  A) Accept the orders, checking customers against Pune's own list, the same way head office orders are checked against head office's list.  B) Refuse the orders until Sharma Traders is also on head office's list.  C) Accept the orders but mark them for a manager to review.
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

2 of 5. An uploaded file lists an order for 'Gupta & Sons' before it lists Gupta & Sons as a customer. Head office handles this case in a set way today. What should Pune do?
  A) Pune follows exactly the same rule as head office. If head office accepts this order of entries, so does Pune. If head office refuses it, so does Pune.  B) Pune accepts the file whatever order the entries are in.  C) Pune always refuses unless the customer is listed first.
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

3 of 5. An uploaded customer, 'Joshi Electricals', is already on Pune's list with an old phone number, and the file brings a new one. What should happen?
  A) Update the existing Pune entry with the new details. Don't create a duplicate, and ignore other branches' lists when matching.  B) Add a second Joshi Electricals entry at Pune with the new number.  C) Stop and ask a person which details are correct.
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

  A) Undo all of them at Pune, leave head office untouched, and show the error.  B) Keep the 319 good orders and only skip the rest.  C) Undo Pune's orders and also pause head office's uploads until it's fixed.
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >
